question: Does the 687-cell numeric reference reproduce the upper classes and lower codes printed on the 1979 chart, and which consumers depend on disagreements?
outcome: All 687 cells visually read. Eight primary codes and one upper class corrected; all 16 old lower-code ambiguities resolved provisionally. Twenty-one numeric row records change, with zero remaining duplicate codes. Explicit-location joins change 11 v1 and eight v3 reference units; v2 has zero direct changes and 18 units requiring identity review. Twenty-one release chart rows and 65/88 stored v1/v2 prediction alternatives are affected.
challenge: Broken ink confuses 5, 6 and 8; old alternatives and duplicate primary labels make global code replacement unsafe. Model-service interruptions and a saved erroneous 571 decision required recovery and additional inspection.
remedy: Preserved first-pass observations, rendered every cell at 8 pixels per point, reinspected 57 cells at 16 or 24, recorded digit features and graphic context, joined consumers by cell identity, and retained preliminary exploratory outputs locally before the final 671 correction.
retry_when: An independent reviewer or expert can confirm the printed digits, particularly 333, 360, 698 and 671; consumer owners can resolve unlocated candidate identities and freeze a new sensitivity scoring run and release version.
